default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: Indicates the existence of an object or event at a location (there is/are...)
There is a notice about the summer festival in the classroom.
A relative clause modifying a noun (a person who is going...)
Those going to the summer festival, please gather at the station at 14:00.
Follows a clause indicating a cause or reason (because...)
Since there is no place to park bicycles in the park, please use trains or other means of transportation.
there is/are not, do not have
Indicates a change into another day or state: become..., change into...
If it rains, the summer festival will be held on July 22 (Saturday) instead.
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Indicates the existence or location of an object or place: be located...
My house is in the countryside.
exist, be located; used for inanimate objects and places
Used to list reasons, qualities, or characteristics: and..., besides...
Indicates an estimated degree or amount: about, approximately (about two hours)
Used with a negative form to mean “not... much” or “hardly...”
It takes about two hours by car to reach the town with a department store and a movie theater, and there are hardly any fashionable shops or restaurants either.
Indicates a time or period in the past: when, back when...
Past negative form of a な-adjective: did not like...
Therefore, when I was a child, I did not like the countryside.
indicates a change of state (to become, to grow)
describes a gradual change continuing from the past to the present (gradually becoming…)
However, as I grew up, I gradually came to like this countryside.
to like, to be fond of
to realize or notice something/a fact
placed at the end of a sentence to explain a reason or cause (it is because…)
That is because I realized that the countryside has many good points.
realized, noticed (past form of 気がつく)
comparison pattern meaning “not as…as” (A is not as…as B)
conjunction expressing contrast or concession (but, however)
used to list additional characteristics or reasons (not only…but also…)
The countryside is not as convenient as the town, but it is quiet, and the water and vegetables are also very delicious.
pattern expressing strong liking for the object marked by が
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: pattern indicating that an object or event exists at a location (there is…at/in…)
There is a notice at the library entrance.
honorific form of a Group 3 verb (利用する → 利用される), showing respect toward library users
particle marking the intended recipient of information (to…, for…)
For those who use the library
expresses completing an action (読み終わった: finished reading)
polite pattern for requesting or asking someone to do something (please…)
➤ After finishing a book, please return it to the reception desk.
V-たら: after doing V1, do V2
➤ After using the desks and chairs, be sure to tidy them up.
V-て + 帰る: do something and then return, taking it along
Please take the trash home with you.
V-る + ときは: when doing something
V-てから: after doing something, then do the next action
➤ When copying a book, tell the reception desk first, then make the copies.
〜ないでください: polite request not to do something
➤ Please do not do the following things inside the library.
〜たり〜たりする: list representative actions
V-る + こと: nominalizes a verb, meaning “the act of V-ing”
V-る + こと: nominalizes a verb, meaning “the act of V-ing”
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: A plain-form clause modifies the following noun (the email Tanaka sent).
This is the email that Tanaka sent to Kim.
Conveys information heard from someone else (“I heard that…”).
I heard that Kim is currently in Korea.
Marks the starting and ending points (“from … to …”).
Expresses the speaker’s intention or plan to do something (“I am planning to…”).
I am planning to go to South Korea from the 23rd to the 27th.
Offers a gentle suggestion or representative example (“such as…,” “something like…”).
A polite invitation or suggestion (“would you like to…?”).
If it is convenient for you, Kim, would you like to have dinner together in the evening?
Someone does something for one’s benefit.
Does something in advance as preparation for the future (“do in advance, reserve ahead”).
If you let me know which day you can go out for a meal, I will reserve a restaurant in advance.
if you do it as a favor
Nominalizes an action (the act of being able to meet someone).
Expresses anticipation or excitement about something upcoming.
I am really looking forward to meeting you in South Korea.
can meet (potential form of 会う)
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: A plain-form clause modifies the noun that follows (here, '留学生が書いた' modifies '作文': an essay written by an international student).
This is an essay written by an international student.
Indicates a point in the past ('two years ago').
I came to Japan two years ago.
Indicates that something happens accidentally or unwillingly, often with a sense of regret (“end up getting filled with trash”).
Indicates a change of state (“become full”).
Therefore, ② the garbage bin at my home quickly ends up full of plastic trash.
Conditional pattern meaning “whenever/if…, then…” (“if one does so, then…”).
Lists multiple characteristics or reasons (“both attractive and convenient”).
③ Indeed, doing so keeps snacks and tomatoes clean and is convenient for people living alone.
Lists representative actions, such as putting things in a bag or placing them in a box.
Pattern expressing that it is not necessary to do something.
Used to express a personal opinion or thought (I think that...).
However, I do not think it is necessary to put each snack and tomato into a plastic bag or plastic container like that.
If plastic or vinyl bags are not used, (...).
Used to list reasons, causes, or similar characteristics ('not only convenient, but also...').
Expresses that something is easy to do ('生活しやすい': easy to live in).
Expresses one's thoughts or impressions in the past ('thought that...').
I thought Japan was a very convenient and comfortable country to live in because it has many convenience stores and supermarkets.
Indicates that a particular matter or fact exists ('there is a matter...').
However, there is one unfortunate thing.①
Nominalizes the preceding clause to explain or clarify the content of the subject ('That is, the fact that...').
That is, there is a lot of garbage.
When doing an action, one notices the result in the following clause ('歩いていると': while walking, one notices...).
Everywhere, all places ('どこもきれい': everywhere is clean).
A conjunction connecting two contrasting or opposing clauses ('but').
When walking around town, there is hardly any garbage and everywhere is clean, but when living in Japan, a lot of garbage is produced.
After performing an action, one discovers an unexpected result in the following clause ('when I opened the box, I found...').
Describes a state that continued at the time the speaker observed it ('was in the bag').
For example, when I bought some sweets and opened the box, I found that each piece was individually wrapped in a plastic bag.
was contained in, was packed in
Expresses an inevitable cause-and-effect relationship: whenever this action is performed, that consequence occurs ('eating one causes the garbage to increase by one').
Describes an unwanted event, with a sense of regret ('unfortunately, more garbage ends up increasing').
Every time I eat one sweet, the amount of garbage increases by one piece.
When doing something, one notices the event in the following clause ('when I bought tomatoes, I found...').
Describes a state resulting from an intentional human action ('placed in advance', 'wrapped in advance').
The other day, when I bought tomatoes at the supermarket, I found them placed in a plastic container and already wrapped in plastic.
Connects actions occurring in chronological order (“go home and then cook…”).
both A and B (“both plastic trays and plastic bags”).
When I get home and cook, both the plastic container and the plastic wrapping become garbage.
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: After doing something, one discovers an event or result (“When ... came home, ...”).
Describes a state resulting from an intentional action performed earlier (“had been placed”).
Describes going somewhere and then returning to the original location (“come home from school”).
When Mika came home from school, this note had been placed on the desk.
Placed after the recipient’s name at the beginning of a letter or note (“To ...”).
Indicates the purpose of movement (remove masu from the V-masu form + に行く: “go to do something”).
Do something and then return (“go buy things and come back”).
I’m going to buy some things and will be back.
States a cause or reason objectively and gently (“because / since...”).
Indicates a temporal condition or sequence (“after finishing V1, do V2”).
Makes a polite request, suggestion, or permission (“please eat them”).
There are grapes in the refrigerator, so please eat them after you finish your homework.
Someone performs an action for the benefit of the speaker or someone in the speaker’s family (“send for someone”).
Grandma sent the grapes to us.
Invitation or suggestion for the listener to do something together: “let's ...”
Call someone by phone; the recipient is marked with に.
Placed after the sender's name at the end of a letter or message: “From ...”
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Purpose of movement: go somewhere to do something (V-masu stem + に行く/行きました).
The other day, I went to eat ramen with a friend.
Be just about to do something (volitional form + とする).
Familiar request or reminder meaning “please don't do ...” (V-nai + で).
Describes an action in progress at a point in the past.
Just as I was about to eat the ramen, my friend said, “Wait a moment! Don't eat yet!” and took lots of pictures of the ramen.
Finish doing something (V-masu stem + 終わる).
Expresses regret or an unwanted outcome that has occurred.
Expresses a change of state: become ... (おいしくなくなる: become no longer delicious).
By the time my friend finished taking pictures, the hot ramen had gone cold and was no longer delicious.
expresses a gradual change progressing from the past to the present (increasing more and more)
Recently, more and more people have started taking photos before eating.
should do something (expresses what is naturally, reasonably, or morally expected)
expresses a wish for someone not to do something
expresses the speaker's thoughts or personal opinion
I think food should be eaten when it is at its most delicious, so I wish people would not do things like that.
want someone not to do something
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: expresses an action in progress at the time of speaking (be doing something)
I am shopping on the Internet.
honorific passive form expressing respect for the customer's action
used after a noun to indicate the recipient or addressee of a notice or letter (to, for)
conditional pattern meaning “if/when... then...,” expressing an inevitable result after a condition
If you buy 3,000 yen or more, there is no shipping fee.
does not cost, is free of charge
humble potential form: can do ... for someone
■ We can deliver the product three days after you place your order.
three days later, after three days
honorific form for Group 3 verbs used with Sino-Japanese verbal nouns, showing respect for the customer's action
■ If you use the service that delivers your order the day after it is placed, there is a 300-yen charge.
in the case of doing V; when doing V
■ If you would like to include a message card, there is a 100-yen charge.
negative potential pattern: cannot do N; N cannot be carried out
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: when, at the time of — identifies when an action takes place
expresses a habit or a regularly repeated action
I always sing whenever I drive a car.
If/when..., then... (indicates a necessary or likely consequence).
End up doing something (expresses regret or concern about an unwanted result).
However, my mother says that if I sing while driving, I might cause an accident, so I should stop doing it.
If it is... (with a noun, presents a hypothetical condition).
And; because... (lists multiple reasons or qualities).
When I am in the car, singing is not too noisy, and it also makes me feel very happy.
So that; in order to (indicates a purpose aimed at achieving a desired state).
Have experienced something (with the negative form, means “have never done it”).
I think that... (expresses a personal thought or opinion).
However, I am careful not to cause an accident, and since I have never caused one even once, I think everything is fine.
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Describes doing something elsewhere and then bringing it or returning with it to the speaker’s location.
「私が買ってきた」modifies the noun 「おみやげ」, meaning “the souvenir I bought and brought.”
The souvenir I had bought and brought was wine.
V-stem + ながら: performing two actions simultaneously (e.g., drinking and eating)
〜で (みんなで): indicates the manner or number of people carrying out an action together
In my country, everyone eats a meal together while drinking wine.
Potential form (negative): cannot drink, due to one's constitution or alcohol tolerance
〜し、〜: lists reasons, conditions, or characteristics in parallel
〜てはいけません: expresses prohibition or that something is not allowed
However, Yamada's parents cannot drink alcohol, and Yamada and his younger sister are still not allowed to drink alcohol.
must not drink, be not allowed to drink
〜と思いました: quotes the speaker's thoughts at that time, directly or indirectly
I thought, 「失敗した」: “I've messed up.”
〜なら: gives an opinion or advice based on a topic that has been raised
〜と思いました: expresses a past thought or judgment
I thought that if I bought a souvenir, (...).
〜から: indicates a reason or cause
〜と言って: quotes what someone said
〜てくれました: indicates that someone did something beneficial or helpful for the speaker, with a sense of gratitude
But Yamada's family said they were happy because it was a rare wine, and they were delighted to receive it.
Lists representative actions, such as making and eating sweets, playing games, and chatting.
The て-form connects actions that occur in sequence, such as making something and then eating it.
Then, the whole family made and ate takoyaki together, played games, and talked a lot.
An い-adjective directly modifies the noun that follows it, as in “an enjoyable day.”
The polite past form of a noun sentence, meaning “was a day...”.
It was a very enjoyable day.
go somewhere in order to do something
Last week, I went to Yamada's house to visit.
gives an objective reason or cause (because it is far...).
expresses obligation or necessity, must do something (must take a train and a bus).
Yamada's house is far from my apartment, so I have to use a train and a bus.
nominalizes a verb (the act of using a train and a bus).
conditional or hypothetical pattern (if I get it wrong...).
expresses uncertainty or worry about what to do.
Since it was my first time using a train and a bus, I was very worried: 「もし、電車とバスを間違えたらどうしよう」.
if I make a mistake, if I get it wrong
expresses a cause-and-effect relationship or an immediately following action (as soon as I finished telling...).
indirect request or asking someone to do something (asking their father to come pick someone up).
someone does something beneficial for the speaker or someone close to them.
When I told Yamada about ①that matter, Yamada asked their father to come by car to pick me up at my apartment.
come to pick someone up as a favor
asked someone to do something as a favor
Expresses gratitude when someone does something beneficial for the speaker (here, agreeing on the speaker’s behalf).
Yamada's father immediately said, 「②もちろん、いいよ」.
Indicates that when someone arrives, the following event occurs immediately afterward.
Another person’s welcoming action expresses hospitality toward the speaker.
When I arrived at Yamada’s house, Yamada’s mother and younger sister, who was a high school student, came out to welcome me.
Perform an action elsewhere and then bring something back or return (buying a gift and bringing it along).
A pattern used to invite or encourage someone to do something together (let’s drink together).
I gave Yamada’s family a souvenir I had bought in my home country and said, “Let’s drink together.”
Indicates an outwardly visible facial expression or emotion (a troubled expression).
Then, ③ everyone looked a little troubled.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: To receive something from someone; the polite past form is used here.
A person participating in the town-cleaning volunteer activity received this note.
To..., addressed to...; used in the heading of a message or letter to indicate the recipient.
To everyone involved in the cleaning volunteer activity,
Introduces a premise or background before presenting the main point.
Indicates a cause or reason: because construction or repair work is underway.
The negative potential form of “to use,” meaning “cannot use.”
Regarding the town-cleaning volunteer activity held every Saturday, the park where everyone usually gathers is unavailable because construction is underway.
not A but B; negates the first option in favor of the second
decide to do something, decide on something intentionally
Therefore, starting next week, we have decided to use the parking lot in front of the station as our meeting place instead of the park.
The time is the same as usual.
polite request, favor, or instruction: please...
connects two actions in chronological order: do V, then do V
Please come to the parking lot at 9 a.m. with a garbage bag.
nominalizes a clause: the thing or matter that...; for example, something that is unclear
polite request or suggestion: please contact...
If there is anything you do not understand, please contact Tanaka.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: say that, think that; quotes an opinion or thought
Some people say that alcohol is bad for the body, so they do not drink.
can do; be able to do something
say that; think that... (quoting someone else's opinion)
However, some people say that drinking alcohol improves their mood and can reduce stress.
continue doing something; keep doing something (verb stem + 続ける)
do things such as...; listing representative actions
let's...; a suggestion, invitation, or appeal
However, avoid drinking alcohol every day or drinking a large amount at one time.
do V2 without doing V1; without doing...
way of doing something (verb stem + 方)
please do...; polite request or advice
Also, drinking only alcohol without eating anything is bad for your body, so please be careful.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: describes a state resulting from a deliberate prior action (置いてある: has been placed in advance).
This note had been placed on Yamakawa's desk.
The divider line marks the beginning of the message.
Used after the recipient’s name at the beginning of a letter or message: “To...”
Added after an adjective to express an excessive degree: too cramped.
Indicates an objective, polite reason or cause: because...so...
A polite request asking someone to do something for you: could you...for me?
The room for today’s meeting is far too cramped, so could you have us change to a slightly larger room?
could you change it for me?
A modifying clause placed before a noun: a computer used for the meeting.
Doing something in advance to prepare for the future: will prepare in advance.
I will prepare the computer to be used for the meeting in advance.
Nominalizes an action: the act of photocopying.
Someone does something for you, expressing gratitude: helped me.
Tanaka helped me copy the materials.
Doing something in advance to prepare or maintain a state: will leave ready.
I will leave the materials on the desk in advance.
will place in advance, will leave ready
Expresses a judgment or prediction about something likely to happen soon: looks like it will run long.
A conjunction expressing a mild transition or contrast: but.
A form used to invite or encourage someone to do something together: let’s...
Today’s meeting looks like it will run long, but let’s do our best.
looks like it will run long
The dividing line marking the end of the message.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: 〜から: marks the starting point of an action in time (from last month).
I started a part-time job at a zoo last month.
〜たり、〜たりする: lists representative actions that make up a job (guiding visitors and explaining animals).
〜について: indicates a specific topic or subject (about animals).
Vる＋ことです: defines or explains the content of something (the job is doing...).
My job is to guide visitors who come to the zoo and explain animals to them.
〜ように（目的）: indicates a goal or purpose (so that the children can understand).
〜ながら: describes two actions taking place simultaneously (showing pictures while talking).
〜ようにしている: expresses an effort to make a habit of doing something (trying to speak clearly).
For children, I show them pictures and photographs of animals while trying to explain things in an easy-to-understand way, so that they can learn various things about animals.
〜が: connects two clauses with a contrast (although busy, it is enjoyable).
Vて（理由）: the て-form indicates the reason for a resulting feeling (being able to meet them makes the speaker happy).
I am busy every day, but I am very happy because I get to see cute animals.
get to meet; be able to meet
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: indicates an action continuing throughout the time another action is taking place (while listening...)
Japanese people give frequent backchannel responses while listening to someone speak.
give verbal responses while listening, nod in agreement
defines or explains the meaning of a concept (“A means B”).
lists representative actions (“doing things such as saying... and nodding...”)
Aizuchi means repeatedly saying “yeah, yeah,” “oh, really?” or “that’s right,” or moving one’s head up and down.
give verbal responses while listening, nod in agreement
quotes or specifies particular content (“that...”; “with the content that...”)
indicates the purpose for which something is used (“something used for...”)
Aizuchi is used to convey the messages “I’m listening to you” and “Please go on.”
Masu-stem + 終わる: finish or complete an action (finish speaking).
Advice that someone should not do something
However, in some cultures abroad, people believe that when listening to someone, one should look the other person in the eyes and say nothing until they have finished speaking.
Indicates that there are occasional cases in which something happens (“if there is an opportunity/case to converse”).
Verb stem + 続ける: to continue or persist in an action (“keep saying”).
If that person happens to have a conversation with a Japanese person, the foreigner speaking may find it noisy and annoying because the Japanese listener keeps saying things like 「うん、うん」 and 「はい、はい」.
if there is; if it happens
Expresses an unintended resulting state or feeling (“end up feeling uneasy”).
Softly and politely expresses a personal thought or opinion (“I think perhaps ...”).
Conversely, when Japanese people are speaking, I think they often end up feeling uneasy because the foreigner does not give aizuchi.
be talking; be having a conversation
Connects two clauses showing an inevitable relationship (“when ...; whenever ...”).
When cultures differ, methods of communication differ as well.
Advice to do something; should consider the method.
Nominalizes the preceding clause: “the fact that the method of conveying differs.”
Therefore, Japanese people and foreigners should understand that the way of conveying the message 「（　　　）」 differs, and consider how to communicate accordingly.
Expresses a well-founded belief or supposition: “should certainly be...”
Potential form of する: “can communicate.”
If we do that, we should be able to communicate comfortably and pleasantly, whether or not we give responsive nods.
even if one gives a responsive remark
even if one does not give a responsive remark
